column1: # facts/anchors.tsv -- where in echovr.exe each value can be read back.
# Found with the IDA extraction at authoring time; VERIFIED at test time by
# reading echovr.exe, so the shipped guard has no database dependency.
# b       ALWAYS the length of instr_bytes, for every kind.  It said "width b" for disp32,
#         which reads as the 4-byte field width, and a contributor who followed that
#         produced rows whose failure blamed the binary for a defect in the row.  The
#         field width comes from `kind`; b is how many bytes get read back and compared.
# a       for disp*/imm*/riprel, the byte index of the field INSIDE instr_bytes.
#         for vtslot, a displacement from anchor_va.  Unused by the other kinds.
# kind    disp8/disp32  instruction at anchor_va encodes the offset at byte [a]
#         imm8/imm32    instruction at anchor_va carries the constant at byte [a]
#         riprel        instruction at anchor_va RIP-addresses the fact; disp32 at [a]
#         instr_at      the fact IS anchor_va; instr_bytes must match the file there
#         u32_at        four bytes at anchor_va are the fact
#         vtslot        qword at anchor_va + a is the fact
